P	Five days north of Stonetop via the <b>Highway</b> (page 270), after winding through the <b>Foothills</b> (page 144) and climbing into the <b>Whitefang Mountains</b> (page 480), you'll come to a pass between two rocky slopes. The pass is blocked by a mighty wall, with dwellings and grander structures on the cliffs above.
P	Long ago, this was the southernmost outpost of the <b>Rime Lords</b> (page 316).
P	Today, it is home to descendants of their disciples. They are a stoic, unfriendly people who want little to do with those from the south. In Stonetop, they tell tales of folk coming down from Barrier Pass to trade ancient wonders for goats or grain, but none alive remember such a visit.
H2	Questions
HR
Q	According to the tales, what did the last visitors from Barrier Pass bring to trade, all those years ago?
Q	When was the last time anyone from Stonetop tried to trade with Barrier Pass? Were they ignored? Chased off? Or what?
Q	What went wrong when villagers last crossed paths with a party from Barrier Pass up in the Foothills?
Q	Who do you know (in Gordin's Delve, perhaps) who hails from Barrier Pass or beyond? Why did they leave?
Q	What do you think lies past that great big wall?
Q	Who or what do you think they put in those cages that line the Highway as one approaches?
Q	Why do you think their warriors carry only blunt weapons?
P	If a PC has visited Barrier Pass, or beyond:
Q	What brought you there in the first place?
Q	Why did they let you in?
Q	What surprised you the most about how they live?
Q	What taboo or point of etiquette did you run afoul of? How so?
Q	Do they worship the same gods up there? If so, how does that worship differ from down here in Stonetop?
PAGE	27
H2	Places
HR
B	<b>The approach</b>: after winding up switchbacks, the Highway straightens and enters a wide pass with steep rocky slopes on either side.
B	<b>Large cages line the slopes</b>, swinging in the wind, filled with human (?) bones or starved, raving prisoners.
B	<b>The Wall</b>, grand and implacable, 50 feet tall and 20 feet wide, spanning the width of the pass.
B	<b>A gate in the Wall</b>, closed of course, the Highway ending 50 feet before it.
B	<b>The East Slope</b>, dotted with dwellings, stables, and terraced gardens, all connected with narrow stairs and switchback paths.
B	<b>A waterfall</b> pours down the east slope, north of the wall. Diverted to gardens and cisterns.
B	<b>The West Slope</b>, featuring old giantscale structures, now used as dormitories, kitchens, and so forth for monks and guardians.
B	<b>The Great Hall</b>, its façade elaborately decorated, leading into a vast chamber carved from a mountain cavern. Where residents gather, meditate, train.

H2	People
HR
P	The people of Barrier Pass descend from the <b>Rime Lords</b>' (page 316) mortal disciples. Their names are Nepalese- and Tibetan-inspired (see page 483).
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The Three Honorable Sages</b> are powerful <b>adepts</b> (page 328) who preside over Barrier Pass. Each leads one of the three sects.
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The Empty Sky sect</b> values preservation and stillness; its monks spend much time in meditative stasis. Led by <b>Gar</b>
P	<b>Torjeng</b> (<b>Instinct</b> to avoid disruption and distraction).
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The Unmoved Mountain sect</b> teaches extreme ascetic disciplines, pushing adherents to continually test themselves. Led by <b>Preshi Kav</b> (<b>Instinct</b> to drive her students towards perfection).
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The White Crystal sect</b> is devoted to order. The majority of guardians and layfolk follow this sect. Its few monks often lead patrols, mete out justice in nearby farms, and hunt monsters. Led by <b>Oparma Div</b> (<b>Instinct</b> to tame chaos).
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Monks from each sect</b> dwell in the fortress, ranging wildly in experience and aptitude. (~40 total, including novices)
ICON	icons/people.svg
P	The <b>Guardians</b> are sworn to defend Barrier Pass. Many are failed monks.
P	They bear ancient bronze shields and armor, but wield no edged weapons. (~20 total)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The rest of the inhabitants</b> are lay folk: families and individuals who garden, herd, cook, clean, and otherwise keep the fortress-monastery running. (~140 souls total)

H3	Stoic and unfriendly
P	Why are the people of Barrier Pass so unwelcoming or even hostile to southerners?
P	That's for you and your table to decide, but perhaps…
E	<b>Aratis</b> herself (page 22) charged them to preserve the Rime Lords' teachings, and eschew the debased peoples of the south;
E	their ancestors fought off the <b>Barrow</b> <b>Builders</b> (page 34) and they still hold a grudge;
E	one of the thirteen surviving <b>Rime</b> <b>Lords</b> (page 316) is hidden in their mountain chambers;
E	a prophecy foretells doom coming from the south;
E	the fortress is tainted by <b>Y'aaw'kara</b> (page 421), and any who dwell here must guard against the <b>Howling Curse</b> (page 492);
E	some combination of the above; or
E	something completely different.
TH	steading improvement
C	<b>TRADE WITH</b> Surely it would benefit both communities were we to trade with each other!
P	Requires getting them to talk to you in the first place, which requires 1 of these:
C	Bringing them a valuable artifact of the Rime Lords, as a gift or to trade
C	A resident in good standing, vouching for you
P	And then, all of the following:
C	Making a compelling offer
C	Convincing at least two of the Honored Sages to accept
C	Two successful trade missions, each in a different season
P	When you <b><i>mark all the requirements</i></b>, increase Fortunes by 1 and add "Trade with Barrier Pass (timber, ivory, parchment, fine wool, goats, sheep)".
P	Henceforth, when <b><i>spring bursts forth</i></b> <b><i>and Stonetop has at least 1 Surplus</i></b>,
P	Stonetop gains +1 Surplus from trade. Also, when you <b><i>Trade & Barter</i></b> <b><i>for timber, ivory, fine wool, goats,</i></b> <b><i>sheep, parchment, vellum, or ink</i></b>, you have advantage.

H3	Commonly available
P	The following are special items in Stonetop, but commonly available in Barrier Pass—PCs can acquire them here without having to roll. They do need to trade something of equal Value. Crops and produce are usually in demand.

If they wish to acquire or sell a bladed weapon, they have disadvantage. <b>On</b> <b>a 6-</b>, they don't mark XP, and it's just not available/no one is interested—they might have better luck with a nearby farm or band of mammoth herders.

TH	trade opportunities
P	If the PCs get a trade opportunity (from the Seasons Change move),
P	Barrier Pass might offer the following:
B	A fair exchange of goods, plus someone to vouch for them should they wish for future trade (see <b>Trade with Barrier Pass</b>, page 29).
B	A good exchange rate, two or even three Value 2 items for 1 Surplus.
B	Two or three ivory mammoth tusks (Value 3), in exchange for help with a problem.
B	A Value 3 mundane item, in exchange for some less-valuable artifact of the Rime Lords
B	<b>Dark ice</b> (page 322) in substantial quantities
B	An arcanum from the <b>Rime Lords</b> (page 322), the <b>spirits of the</b> <b>wild</b> (page 364), or <b>death and</b> <b>the undying</b> (page 74).
PAGE	32
H2	Secrets
HR
B	Secret paths/doors lead in and out of the compound. Outsiders are blindfolded when taken through them, or condemned to death if they learn of their existence.
B	There is a hidden vault deep in the mountainside, protected by all manner of magics and <b>tulpas</b> (page 324). Only a few inhabitants know it exists; fewer know what it contains.
B	One of the monks has started down the path of becoming a <b>false adept</b> (page 329). She is popular and (apparently) quite talented. Only Preshi Kav (Honored Sage of the Unmoved Mountain) suspects anything.
H2	Hooks
HR
B	The PCs acquire an artifact of the Rime Lords; maybe they can leverage it into opening trade negotiations?
B	A party from Barrier Pass comes to Stonetop, offering ivory/gold/arcana for food/livestock; they are tightlipped, haunted, on edge.
B	A condemned criminal escapes from Barrier Pass and seeks refuge; a <b>shantyara</b> (page 495) pursues them.
H2	Dangers
H3	Surroundings
B	Steep, treacherous, rocky slopes
B	<b>Harsh mountain weather</b> (page 488)
B	<b>Hypothermia & frostbite</b> (page 489), if you stay out in the cold
B	<b>Rockslides</b> (page 376) or <b>avalanches</b> (page 489) in winter
H3	Fortifications
B	Minor <b>tulpas</b> (page 324) watching the approach, warning the fortress of visitors
B	A wall of smooth stone, 50 feet tall and 20 feet wide
B	Walkways and crenelations atop the wall
B	A final approach, 50 feet or so with no protection from the Makers' Roads
B	A massive gate of wood and bronze
B	Beyond the gate, a barbican lined with murder holes
B	Cleverly concealed doors that open only from the inside
B	A pair of <b>khyagseng</b> (page 326) guarding the entrance to the Great Hall
H3	Folk from elsewhere
B	<b>Mammoth herders</b> (page 177) or <b>valley farmers</b> (page 484), here to trade, pay tribute, or seek redress
B	An <b>adept</b> (page 328), visiting from another fortress-monastery or some cave in the wilds
B	A <b>mkhalang</b> (page 327), claiming to bring tidings but really just stirring up trouble
B	A <b>bandit</b> (page 131) or criminal from one of the nearby farm valleys, condemned to death, pleading for mercy
B	A <b>spirit of the wild</b> (page 356), come to visit or debate with the Honored Sages
B	A <b>thrall</b> of the Things Below (page 435), here under false pretense, urged to spread chaos and woe

P	• Endure or absorb raw elemental power
P	• Refuse to adapt or change

P	• Take charge
P	• Do their duty
P	• Suppress the emotions of others
